transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hey Doc. Yeah, well... I guess I came in because, man, I just can't stop. It's like... you know when you leave a truck running in the driveway? Just idling but vibrating and ready to go? That's me, all day long. I got this motor running inside me, just humming and revving up from the minute my eyes open. And it's getting to where I can't stand it, because if I have to just sit still... like, man, even just sitting out there in your waiting room a minute ago? I thought I was gonna jump right out of my skin. I kept having to stand up, look at the wall, pace around a little bit. 

It's like that everywhere I go. If I have to sit still at church, or if I'm just at home trying to sit on the couch, or like I said, here at the clinic... I get this awful feeling like I'm completely trapped. Like I'm locked in a tight little box or something and the walls are closing in. I just absolutely have to get up. I have to go do something, mess with something, walk around the yard, whatever. I just can't be still. It's exhausting, honestly, but I can't turn the motor off, no matter how hard I try, and I just... I don't know how regular people just sit in chairs for more than five minutes. I really don't.
Can you describe if you often feel physically restless or like you have to move around even when you're trying to relax?

Yeah, exactly! That's exactly it. Even when I’m really, really trying to just... you know, be respectful and pay attention. Like, I was down at the assistance office a couple weeks back, just trying to get some paperwork sorted out since I ain't working right now, and the lady across the desk is talking to me. I'm telling myself, 'Just sit still, listen to what she's saying, don't mess this up.' But man, my leg... it's just going a mile a minute. Bouncing up and down like it's got a spring in it, shaking the whole floor. 

And if it ain't my leg, it's my hands. I just can't let my hands rest in my lap like a normal person. I was tapping my fingers on the arm of the chair—just tap, tap, tap, tap—until the lady gave me this look. So I tried to stop that, put my hands in my lap, but then two seconds later I realize I grabbed this paperclip off her desk and I’m just twisting it. Bending it back and forth, twisting it all up in my hands the whole entire time we're talking until the metal just snaps. 

It's like the energy just has to leak out of my fingers and my toes. I try to be polite, because my momma raised me right and I know how you're supposed to act in an office, but my body just doesn't care. If I'm not twisting something, I'm rolling up the edge of my shirt, or picking at the seam of my jeans, or my foot is doing some crazy drum solo. Even at home on the couch, just trying to watch a movie and relax, my leg shakes the whole furniture. My buddy told me I was making him seasick just sitting next to me! It just never stops, doc, no matter how hard I try to just be still.

latest_inference.note: The patient's description of persistent physical restlessness, inability to remain still, and associated distress is most consistent with Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Hyperactive-Impulsive Presentation. Other anxiety or movement-related diagnoses were considered but are less likely given the chronic motor restlessness without prominent anxiety, trauma history, obsessive features, or isolated situational triggers.

This presentation could indicate a variety of conditions, including anxiety disorders, obsessive-compulsive and related disorders, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, or even certain psychomotor disturbances seen in other mental or neurologic conditions. No specific disorder can be ruled in or out yet based on this initial narrative.
